sections.h2: Where is the Lackawanna County Recorder of Deeds, and when can I record a deed?
sections.html:
The office sits at 123 Wyoming Avenue, Suite 218, in Scranton, and the number is 570-963-6775. Hours run from 9:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m., but the counter stops taking documents for recording at 3:45 p.m.

A signed deed can reach the office three ways: carried in, dropped in the box in the main lobby of the Government Center, or sent by U.S. Mail. Title companies often skip all three and file electronically through Simplifile, CSC or ePN, the vendors the county lists on its Recorder of Deeds page.

The Recorder records and indexes property documents, and it also collects realty transfer tax for the state, the municipality and the school district. Anyone selling a house in Lackawanna County meets this office on the last day of the sale, after the deed has been signed and notarized at closing.

sections.h2: What must a Lackawanna County deed contain before it is recorded?
sections.html:
It has to meet the county's written recording requirements, which have followed national PRIA document standards since September 1, 2024. Missing items are the usual reason a closing package gets sent back.

  • Paper size of 8.5 by 11 inches (8.5 by 14 is tolerated), type no smaller than 12 point, and margins of at least one inch on every page.
  • Original signatures in dark ink. Handwriting is not allowed anywhere else on the page, and highlighter marks are not allowed at all.
  • A complete legal description naming the municipality, county and state, plus the county tax parcel number. The Assessment Office certifies each parcel number before the deed is recorded, and mailed packages are forwarded there first.
  • A formal acknowledgment before a notary or another authorized officer, showing the date, the signer's name, the notary's signature and the expiration date.
  • A Certificate of Residence signed by the buyer, giving a precise address.
  • Written dollar amounts that match the numbers, since consideration is checked against the transfer tax paid.

A deed cannot be fixed by re-recording it. Errors are corrected with a Corrective Deed, which must carry a Statement of Value, an explanation, and a full copy of the deed being corrected.

sections.h2: How do I pay the Lackawanna County Recorder, and what happens with an overpayment?
sections.html:
Pay by check for the exact amount. The office's requirements sheet says it does not accept credit cards and does not refund overages, and it asks that the submitter's address be printed on every check.

Make checks payable to the Lackawanna County Recorder of Deeds. A check whose memo line points to some other land document is refused, and the office may ask for ID to confirm the address on a check.

Base recording amounts depend on page, name and parcel counts. The county posts a fee calculator on its Recorder page, so run the deed through it, or call before you write the check.

sections.h2: How is realty transfer tax handled on a Lackawanna County sale?
sections.html:
The Recorder collects it when the deed is recorded. Pennsylvania sets the state rate at 1 percent of the value, and the Department of Revenue makes buyer and seller jointly responsible for it. Local shares go to the municipality and school district on top of that.

Some transfers escape the tax, including certain family transfers and property passing by will or intestacy. Even then the Recorder wants the exemption stated in the deed or on a fully completed Statement of Value.

  • When land lies in more than one municipality, the deed must give each municipality's percentage and dollar amount in whole numbers, backed by a Statement of Value.
  • A deed that recites the wrong location is the submitter's problem: the right tax must be paid to the right municipality, and the refund from the wrong one has to be chased by the submitter.
  • Easements also need a Statement of Value, and it counts toward the page total.

sections.h2: What changed in Lackawanna County recording fees in late 2025 and 2026?
sections.html:
Two things. A state budget change signed on November 12, 2025 raised the court-related surcharge on every recording, so the combined court and AOPC portion went from $40.25 to $41.25. The Recorder began collecting the higher amount on November 17, 2025, and packages mailed in with the old amount were sent back to be redone.

Second, since January 1, 2026, attachments on e-recorded documents, such as a Corrective Deed or Deed of Trust, cost an extra $0.50 per page, because the office must print them for the Department of Revenue. Documents brought in, dropped off or mailed do not pick up that per-page charge.

Anyone who prepares a closing package from an older checklist should ask the office for the current total before sending a check.

sections.h2: How did the Lackawanna County reassessment change things for sellers?
sections.html:
The county finished its first full reassessment in nearly 60 years in 2025, moving values off 1968 levels to current market values. A court ordered it after a 2022 resident lawsuit, and the Assessment Office says the county millage rate fell from 89.98 to 5.79 mills to keep the change revenue-neutral.

The county describes the result as roughly a third of owners paying more, a third paying less and a third about the same. A quarterly payment option was introduced for property tax bills. For a seller, the practical point is that an old tax bill says little about what a buyer will pay, so pull the current assessment record before you list.

The appeal deadline for 2027 consideration was August 1, 2026, and the county says appeals open again on April 1, 2027. The Clean & Green application window for 2027 closed June 1, 2026, with the next one starting March 1, 2027. The county also posts a form under Act 29 of 2026 for owners of rentals, LLCs, trusts and other entity-held property bought on or after September 18, 2026.

sections.h2: What is Lackawanna County like for someone selling a house?
sections.html:
Lackawanna County covers 465 square miles in northeastern Pennsylvania, with Scranton as county seat and Carbondale as the other city. It was created on August 13, 1878, the last Pennsylvania county formed, and it grew around anthracite mining and iron and steel. I-81, I-84, I-380 and I-476 all cross it. Twelve public school districts serve it, from Abington Heights and Dunmore to Scranton and North Pocono.

sections.h2: What should I have in hand at a Lackawanna County closing?
sections.html:
A short list heads off most rejections at the counter.

  • The deed, signed in original ink and acknowledged, with the notary stamp clear and nothing typed or written onto it.
  • The county tax parcel number and a full legal description.
  • A signed Certificate of Residence from the buyer.
  • A completed Statement of Value if any tax is excused or the price is not shown on the deed.
  • A check for the exact total, with the submitter's address printed on it.
  • A self-addressed stamped envelope if you want the recorded original mailed back.

Deliver it before 3:45 p.m. on a business day, or have the title company file it electronically.

faqs.q: Can I pay for recording in Lackawanna County with a credit card?
faqs.a: No, according to the office's requirements sheet, which says it does not accept credit cards. Bring a check for the exact amount, made out to the Lackawanna County Recorder of Deeds. A single check may cover both the recording fee and the transfer tax.

faqs.q: What time does Lackawanna County stop recording deeds?
faqs.a: Recording ends at 3:45 p.m. The office stays open until 4:00 p.m., and it opens at 9:00 a.m. A deed that arrives after 3:45 waits for the next business day.

faqs.q: Does a Lackawanna County deed need a parcel number?
faqs.a: Yes. Every document that relates directly to real estate must carry the county tax parcel number, and the Assessment Office certifies it before recording. A mailed package is forwarded to that office for the certification first.

faqs.q: Can a mistake in a recorded deed be fixed by recording it again?
faqs.a: No. The office says deeds can only be corrected with a Corrective Deed. It must include a Statement of Value, a reason for the correction, and a complete copy of the deed being corrected.

faqs.q: Who pays realty transfer tax when a Lackawanna County house sells?
faqs.a: Under Department of Revenue rules, buyer and seller are both liable for the state 1 percent tax. Your sales contract can say who actually pays. The Recorder collects it with the deed and passes it on to the state, the municipality and the school district.
